newsitem.title: GERMANY: German states plan second Jumbo bond issue - paper.
newsitem.headline: German states plan second Jumbo bond issue - paper.

text.p: Several German federal states are likely to issue a second joint "Jumbo" bond in November and appear to be aiming for a volume of three to five billion marks, Handelsblatt reported on Wednesday.
The paper said the bond was expected to have a maturity of five years and may yield five to seven basis points above the 8.25 percent coupon federal government bond maturing in September 2001.
Finance ministry officials from various federal states met on Tuesday to discuss plans for a second issue, the paper said.
Seven of Germany's 16 states, or Laender, launched a joint four billion mark, 10-year Jumbo bond in August in the first pooled state debt issue of its kind.
Handelsblatt said the second Jumbo was likely to be issued by a larger number of states.
The lead-managing banks have urged that mistakes made in the first issue be avoided, Handelsblatt said.

They have demanded more promotion through presentations to investors before the issue, the adoption of an international issue procedure whereby the price is determined by demand -- a process known as fixed price reoffer -- and the appointment of two arrangers as spokesman for the lead managers, the paper said.
The second Jumbo is unlikely to be accompanied by a rating from an international rating agency, the paper said.
